proposals.evidence: Turner specifically places Nepali hāmro, Awadhi hamar, Hindi hamārā and Bhojpuri hamār my in the extended asmāka possessive family. These Nepal/Terai hāmr-/hamār- forms match it, including nominative or singular usages in the survey; the Bhojpuri comparison already documents the shift to my.

proposals.evidence: Turner specifically gives Kumauni tumaro, Nepali timro, Bhojpuri tohār, Hindi tumhārā and Pahari tuãro in the possessive yuṣmad series. The Dotyali and Terai survey forms match these full tumar-/tohar- comparanda; contracted tor- forms are separated because they also match the singular possessive family.

proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly lists Apabhramsha tuhara and Bengali/Oriya tora among possessive derivatives of tuvam, beside Hindi terā. These short tor- singular/low-form Nepal/Terai possessives are assigned to that series; historical overlap with the plural tohar family is acknowledged rather than inferred solely from the generic your gloss.
